newsitem.title: CHINA: HSBC shares drive into record ground.
newsitem.headline: HSBC shares drive into record ground.

text.p: Shares in HSBC Holdings Plc surged deep into record ground on Wednesday, following through on a surge in its share price in overnight trade in London.
The stock jumped HK$15.00 to a record high of HK$269.00 before coming off its highs to trade up HK$12.00 to HK$266.00.
"There is positive sentiment about the bank in London and all the banks did well overnight," said Alan Hutcheson, banking analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
HSBC shares rose HK$5.125 in London to close at HK$259.125.
Dresdner Kleinwort Benson raised its price target for the stock to 24.00 sterling from a previous target of 21.00 sterling.
Ricky Tam, senior research manager at Delta Asia Securities, said the average price earnings ratio for the banking sector in Hong Kong was 20 times and that HSBC was trading at 17 times.
"When you consider the earnings power of HSBC, it can push up further," he said.
HSBC is due to release its interim results on August 4.
Hutcheson said there was also speculation that HSBC would increase its stake in Banco Santiago in Chile.
Chile's Central Bank said it was in talks to sell its option to buy shares in Banco Santiago's forthcoming capital increase to HSBC.
